A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Sparse Autoencoders for Hypothesis Generation. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic and real-world experiments, baseline comparisons, hypothesis discoveries and supporting analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original non-SAE comparisons in Table 7 and researcher evaluations in Figure 2 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The proposed k-sparse autoencoder, L1-based feature selection and LLM interpretation with fidelity-based selection are unchanged. The new Embedding, PCA and Bottleneck variants are evaluation controls, not revisions to the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate WIKI-5, WIKI-15, BILLS, HEADLINES, YELP and CONGRESS. The added ablations reuse the three real-world datasets, and human evaluation assesses existing HEADLINES and CONGRESS hypotheses. Images, proteins and healthcare extensions remain prospective.

E2.justification: Section 6.3 and Table 7 add end-to-end comparisons against direct Embedding features, PCA features and a supervised Bottleneck, substantially expanding controls for the SAE's contribution. BERTopic, NLParam, HypoGeniC and the prior-work novelty comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v3 introduces human evaluation of helpfulness and interpretability: three nonauthor researchers rate significant hypotheses from two datasets in randomized order. New ablation settings include PCA reduction from 1536 to 256 dimensions and a 20-neuron supervised bottleneck. Existing dataset splits and benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v2 already analyzes interpretation fidelity, prompting choices, omitted fidelity validation and losses across pipeline stages. v3 adds controlled non-SAE ablations that test whether the SAE specifically improves interpretation fidelity and nonredundant hypothesis discovery, plus structured human assessment of hypothesis quality.

E5.justification: The new human evaluation specifies three ratings per hypothesis and majority-vote aggregation, adding a limited estimation procedure. Existing Bonferroni corrections, paired t-tests and stochastic interpretation disclosures remain unchanged. No confidence intervals, inter-rater agreement estimates or repeated model-run counts are added.

E6.justification: Existing results in Tables 1–6 and the retained plots are unchanged. New Table 7 reports 45/60 significant SAE hypotheses versus 30/60 for Embedding, and mean fidelity 0.836 versus 0.640 for Bottleneck. Human evaluation adds 24/30 SAE hypotheses rated helpful, 29/30 interpretable and 23 satisfying both, versus at most 7 for a baseline.

T1.justification: The separation and fidelity definitions, Proposition 3.1 and its derivation are unchanged. The proof moves from Appendix E to Appendix F; this is renumbering rather than new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the principal theoretical, methodological and empirical claims. The conclusion modestly qualifies applicability: it explicitly frames the method around text and presents healthcare and protein applications as future extensions, also adding images as a prospective direction.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new ablations as evidence that SAE monosemanticity supports higher-fidelity, less redundant interpretations. It also replaces the earlier sampling rationale with an explanation that weakly activating texts act as hard negatives that improve precision. Existing diagnostic interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies temperature 0 for GPT-4o-mini concept annotation and documents the human-rating questions, evaluator eligibility and aggregation procedure. It supplies configurations for the new controls. Existing SAE hyperparameters, prompts and code, data and demo access information remain.

R1.justification: Related work adds Lam et al. on concept induction and Koh et al. and Feng et al. on concept bottlenecks; the new ablation cites Yang et al. The conclusion adds application references and removes Pierson et al. on health equity. The central positioning relative to hypothesis generation and SAE interpretability is retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized revisions to related work, method explanations, costs and the conclusion, adds a non-SAE ablation subsection and qualitative-evaluation appendix, and expands acknowledgements and funding disclosures. The overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-panel human-evaluation Figure 2 and ablation Table 7, refines the cost-table caption and reflows material. Existing figures and tables retain their displays and results, with subsequent figures renumbered. The conference footer replaces the preprint footer.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens two central validation gaps: matched non-SAE controls test whether the SAE itself provides the benefit, and nonauthor researcher ratings directly assess real-world helpfulness and interpretability beyond predictive significance. These additions support the paper's defining contribution without displacing earlier evidence. The three-rater evaluation covers only two datasets, and aggregate ablation results lack uncertainty estimates, but the evidential improvement is substantial.
